title: Action-Support Likelihood Audits Predict Rollout Consistency Failures in Text-Based World Models

contributions.purpose: Frame and target the world-to-real (W2R) transfer failure problem in text-based world models.
contributions.mechanism: Identifies the W2R transfer problem under policy shift and proposes a support-based diagnostic framework measuring how well rollout actions are supported by the training distribution.
contributions.evaluation: Positioned as a complementary problem to prior world-model work; framework motivated by offline-RL out-of-distribution intuitions (qualitative).
contributions.domain: Text-based (LLM) world models for planning / rollout verification.
contributions.source_quote: We identify the W2R transfer problem in text-based world models and propose a support-based diagnostic framework.

contributions.purpose: Provide a training-free diagnostic that predicts W2R rollout failures.
contributions.mechanism: Enhanced Support-NLL combines three complementary out-of-support signals -- verb frequency (unigram NLL), transition patterns (bigram NLL), and repetition detection -- using only frequency counting from training data, no neural network inference.
contributions.evaluation: On TextWorld with a GPT-4o-mini agent achieves AUROC=0.831 [0.752, 0.901], vs the world model's own observation likelihood (0.587) and action-length baseline (0.447).
contributions.domain: Text-based (LLM) world models for planning / rollout verification.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce Enhanced Support-NLL, combining three complementary out-of-support signals that require no neural network inference.

contributions.purpose: Validate the diagnostic and its components.
contributions.mechanism: Demonstrates performance on TextWorld with ablation studies over the three sub-scores.
contributions.evaluation: AUROC=0.831 on TextWorld; ablations show each sub-score captures distinct failure modes.
contributions.domain: Text-based (LLM) world models for planning / rollout verification.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate AUROC=0.831 on TextWorld, with ablation studies showing each sub-score captures distinct failure modes.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work addresses a complementary problem: given a world model, how can we predict when its rollouts will fail to transfer to the real environment?
Our Enhanced Support-NLL diagnostic draws inspiration from these support constraint ideas, but applies them to predict world model rollout failures rather than to regularize policy learning.

Drawing inspiration from offline reinforcement learning, where out-of-distribution actions cause value overestimation and unreliable dynamics predictions (Kumar et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2020), we hypothesize that actions rare in the training distribution are more likely to cause W2R failures.
